findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC that proves the I1 block is byte-identical to the plan's block, and that the text from 'benign under a code rollback' to the end of §I1 is unchanged from origin/main.
evidence: "replace the ... text ... with the block below, committed exactly as written (same line breaks)"
"The rollback sentence and everything after it stay unchanged, as a new paragraph."
The ACs are all `grep -c` or 'I1 contains' substring checks; none compares the block or the post-rollback tail verbatim.
findings.finding: Step 1 requires the I1 block to be 'committed exactly as written (same line breaks)', and requires the rollback sentence and everything after it to stay unchanged. The ACs only check that about 25 substrings are present. A reflowed, partially paraphrased or partly dropped block (for example, a missing 'It is safe only past causal stability…' sentence, or an altered rollback tail) would still pass.
findings.location: What changes §1 ('committed exactly as written (same line breaks)') vs. Acceptance Criteria
scenarios: An implementer reflows the block or drops the causal-stability sentence, and every AC still passes.
findings.suggested_fix: Save the plan's fenced block to a temp file and run `diff <(awk '/^\*\*`\.retired` lifecycle\.\*\*/,/cc4a23a2405`\)\.$/' docs/concurrency.md) block.md` (prints nothing). Also diff the §I1 tail from the rollback sentence onward against `git show origin/main:docs/concurrency.md`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Say that the hunk-start bounds apply to the old-side (`-a`) line number of each `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` header.
evidence: Every concurrency.md hunk starts at a line from 61 to 80.
Every ADR hunk starts at line 222 or later.
findings.finding: 'Every concurrency.md hunk starts at a line from 61 to 80' does not say whether it means the old-side (`-a`) or new-side (`+c`) start in the `@@` header. The new block is about 40 lines, replacing roughly 15. If git splits the edit into several hunks (for example around identical blank lines), later hunks can start past line 80 on the new side even though the edit stays inside the planned region.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'Only the planned regions change'
scenarios: git diff emits a second hunk with `+95` because a blank line in the middle of the block matches the old text.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword: 'Every concurrency.md hunk's old-side start (`@@ -N`) is between 61 and 80; every ADR hunk's old-side start is ≥ 222.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Diff against the merge-base (`git diff -U0 origin/main...HEAD`) so the scope check sees only this change's edits.
evidence: `git diff -U0 origin/main --stat` lists exactly the 2 files.
Why: 'On origin/main 9d10232dd89'
findings.finding: The scope proof `git diff -U0 origin/main --stat` compares the worktree against the moving tip of origin/main rather than the merge-base. If origin/main moves past 9d10232dd89 before the proof runs, the output includes (reversed) changes from other commits. The '2 files' check would then fail falsely, or hide extra edits.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'Only the planned regions change'
scenarios: Another change merges to main between worktree creation and the AC run, and its files appear in the diff.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD` (three dots) for the file list, and `git diff -U0 origin/main...HEAD` for the hunk-start checks.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Give the exact command for the 'I1 contains' checks, using single-quoted fixed strings (e.g. `sed -n '/^### I1/,/^### I2/p' docs/concurrency.md | grep -cF 'reclaim_collapse`:'`).
evidence: `reclaim_collapse\``
"Each of these greps at least once in I1"
findings.finding: Several 'I1 contains X' ACs give no concrete command; only the first states `grep -c` over the sed output. The module item `reclaim_collapse\`` contains a backtick. If an executor writes it as `grep "reclaim_collapse`"`, the backtick starts command substitution and the grep breaks. The plan needs a concrete, quote-safe fixed-string command.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'I1 names all 7 modules' and the other 'I1 contains' items
scenarios: The shell treats the backtick as command substitution, the grep pattern becomes garbled, and the check passes or fails for the wrong reason.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a template: `sed -n '/^### I1/,/^### I2/p' docs/concurrency.md | grep -cF '<string>'` must print ≥1. For the collapse module, use the anchored string 'reclaim_collapse`:'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make I1 quote the paragraphs' exact titles (or explicitly abbreviate them), and add an AC that I1 contains each quoted title.
evidence: The reconnect and publish protocols are the paragraphs "Reconnect after a history reclaim" and "Publishing a reclaimed baseline" under Inbound — background sync.
`grep -c 'Reconnect after a history reclaim (ADR 0106\|Publishing a reclaimed baseline, and rolling it back' docs/concurrency.md` prints 2
findings.finding: The new I1 text refers to the target paragraphs by shortened names ('Reconnect after a history reclaim', 'Publishing a reclaimed baseline'). The AC greps their actual titles, which include '(ADR 0106' and ', and rolling it back'. So the cross-reference does not match the actual titles. The AC only checks that the paragraphs exist, not that I1's names find them.
findings.location: What changes step 1 block / AC 'I1 points to the 2 existing paragraphs'
scenarios: A reader searches for the quoted title "Publishing a reclaimed baseline" and finds the paragraph only by prefix. The AC passes even if I1 dropped the names entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: In the block, write "Publishing a reclaimed baseline, and rolling it back". Add an AC that I1 contains `Reconnect after a history reclaim` and `Publishing a reclaimed baseline`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly that 'W3 set; W1/W2 filed' is out of scope for this ticket, and name the ticket(s) that own it.
evidence: "docs/concurrency.md §I1 moved 'implemented'; residual pack size quantified; W3 set; W1/W2 filed"
No AC or step mentions W1, W2 or W3.
findings.finding: The Why section quotes the epic's whole acceptance box ('residual pack size quantified; W3 set; W1/W2 filed'), but the plan covers only the I1 move and the residual figure. It never says whether W3, W1 and W2 are handled elsewhere or are out of scope. A reader may then assume this ticket closes the epic box.
findings.location: Why vs What changes / Acceptance Criteria
scenarios: The epic box is ticked when this ticket merges, even though W1/W2 were never filed and W3 never set.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Why: 'This ticket covers only the I1/residual part of the box; W1/W2 filing and W3 are tracked in <ticket ids>.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether ADR 0106's Status header (and its ADR-index entry) changes, and confirm 'specified, in-progress' appears only in the Follow-up paragraph.
evidence: Every ADR hunk starts at line 222 or later.
in the ADR, `grep -c 'specified, in-progress'` prints 0
`make verify` covers the docs-drift, ADR-index and doc-policy tests.
findings.finding: The plan updates only the ADR's Follow-up paragraph. It forbids any ADR hunk before line 222 and limits the diff to exactly 2 files. It never says whether ADR 0106's Status header (and any ADR-index entry checked by the ADR-index test) should still say 'specified' or 'in-progress' once the reclamation is implemented. Two problems follow. If the header also contains 'specified, in-progress', the AC `grep -c 'specified, in-progress'` cannot reach 0. If it says anything else stale, the docs strand an outdated status.
findings.location: What changes step 2 / AC 'The ADR Follow-up is updated' / AC 'Every ADR hunk starts at line 222 or later'
scenarios: The ADR front matter reads 'Status: Accepted (specified, in-progress)', so the AC cannot be satisfied without breaking the line-222 rule.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'ADR 0106 Status header stays <X> (decision status, not implementation status); `grep -n 'specified, in-progress'` on origin/main returns only line 22x.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Use the same epic identifier in the ADR Follow-up as in I1 (slug plus full ID), and give the S1–S3 story IDs if they exist.
evidence: under epic `536b`.
under epic `polite-antivirus-bedbug` (`536b-8930-b922-4063`)
findings.finding: The epic is named in three different ways: the full slug and ID in Why and I1 ('polite-antivirus-bedbug (`536b-8930-b922-4063`)'), but only 'epic `536b`' in the new ADR Follow-up text. The ADR also names stories only as S1/S2/S3, with no ticket IDs.
scenarios: A reader of the ADR cannot resolve 'epic 536b' or 'S1' to a ticket without cross-referencing concurrency.md.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Require that the docs-drift, ADR-index and doc-policy tests pass with no exception, and define 'environmental' (e.g. the same failure reproduces on origin/main) for any other failure.
evidence: `make verify` passes, or each failure is shown to be environmental.
`make verify` covers the docs-drift, ADR-index and doc-policy tests.
findings.finding: '`make verify` passes, or each failure is shown to be environmental' has no definition of 'environmental' and no stated evidence for it. This is the AC the plan relies on for the docs-drift, ADR-index and doc-policy tests, so the escape hatch could excuse a real docs-policy failure.
scenarios: A doc-policy test fails on the new block, and the failure is waved through as 'environmental'.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword: '`make verify` passes; any failure outside the docs tests must reproduce identically on a clean origin/main checkout, with both outputs recorded on the ticket.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State ADR 0106's current header Status and ADR-index entry. If either still says in-progress, include it in the edit set and relax the 'hunk ≥ line 222' AC. Otherwise note that no status line needs changing.
evidence: "docs/adr/0106-remote-anchored-history-reclamation.md: the Follow-up paragraph only."
"Every ADR hunk starts at line 222 or later."
The plan does not mention the ADR's Status field or the ADR index entry.
findings.finding: The plan marks ADR 0106 as implemented only by editing its Follow-up paragraph. The hunk-region AC ('Every ADR hunk starts at line 222 or later') would forbid touching any header Status or front-matter line. The plan does not say whether ADR 0106 has such a line still reading proposed or in-progress. If it does, the ADR would contradict itself after this change: header in-progress, Follow-up implemented.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria → 'Every ADR hunk starts at line 222 or later'; File impact → 'the Follow-up paragraph only'
scenarios: ADR 0106's header reads 'Status: Accepted (in-progress)' or similar, and that line stays stale while the Follow-up claims implemented. The ADR-index and doc-policy tests may or may not catch this.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either move the 2026-11-20 run record and measured residual into ADR 0106 `## Follow-up` (keeping only the durable 'implemented', no-CI-budget and 'grows until next reclaim' statements in §I1), or add one sentence to the plan explaining why the point-in-time figures belong in §I1.
evidence: Block text: 'Measured residual: a fresh blobless bare clone of origin `tickets` at `4fd8b099490` (14,375 commits), taken 2026-11-20 at 21:13 PST, has `size-pack` 122,794 KiB ... The residual grows with write volume until the next reclaim.'
Epic 536b acceptance box: 'docs/concurrency.md §I1 moved 'implemented'; residual pack size quantified; W3 set; W1/W2 filed'. It does not say where the residual must be recorded.
The existing §I1 lines 61-75 contain only doctrine and pointers, with no dated measurements.
The plan has no rationale for placing the run record in I1 instead of the ADR.
findings.finding: The plan puts dated, decaying operational data into the normative §I1 invariant text: run timestamps, before/after SHAs, commit counts, and the residual measurement (122,794 KiB at 4fd8b099490, 14,375 commits). The block itself says 'The residual grows with write volume until the next reclaim', so the figure is stale when it merges. The plan gives no reason for putting this record in I1 rather than in ADR 0106's Follow-up, which is a historical section where point-in-time figures belong. The epic box only asks that the residual be 'quantified', not that it live in I1.
findings.location: What changes §1 (the I1 replacement block, from 'The reclamation was run on 2026-11-20' to the end) and §2 (ADR Follow-up)
scenarios: A reader of the concurrency invariants a month from now reads 122,794 KiB as the current residual, although the pack has grown since.
The next reclaim run needs another edit to the invariant section, so §I1 becomes a changelog.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In ## Why, say that 'W3 set' and 'W1/W2 filed' are already met and cite the evidence (W3 bridge d0bcd620 and the current 102,400 KiB code-checkout budget; W1/W2 ticket ids), so this change completes the acceptance box.
evidence: Plan Why: 'has an acceptance box that reads: "docs/concurrency.md §I1 moved 'implemented'; residual pack size quantified; W3 set; W1/W2 filed". On origin/main 9d10232dd89, two places are out of date'
verify-identity.yml:50 `REBAR_CHECKOUT_PACK_LIMIT_KIB: 102400` (the bridge value 563200 is no longer present)
Epic comments: W1 miserable-pernickety-caudata and W2 hermitical-villainous-damselfly were created; the W3 bridge was merged as d0bcd620 and is tracked for restore by fluorspar-comparable-zeren.
findings.finding: The plan uses the epic acceptance box ('§I1 moved implemented; residual pack size quantified; W3 set; W1/W2 filed') as its reason, but it only addresses the §I1 and residual parts. It never says whether 'W3 set' and 'W1/W2 filed' are already met or what the evidence is. The repo complicates 'W3 set': verify-identity.yml now has REBAR_CHECKOUT_PACK_LIMIT_KIB at 102400, so the 563200 bridge from Gerrit 2392 was reverted when the budget was rescoped to the code checkout. Without that statement, merging this change may not let the box be ticked, so the plan could fix part of the problem while the stated goal stays unmet.
findings.location: ## Why (epic acceptance-box quote) and ## Acceptance Criteria
scenarios: The change merges, but the epic box still can't be ticked because nobody has shown how 'W3 set' applies now that the bridge was reverted.
